title.en: Volume 99 Biographies 37: Tu Danyi, Jia Xuan, Sun Duo, Sun JiKang, Li Ge
title.raw: 卷九十九 列傳第三十七: 徒單鎰 賈鉉 孫鐸 孫即康 李革 Volume 99 Biographies 37: Tu Danyi, Jia Xuan, Sun Duo, Sun JiKang, Li Ge

sentences.zh: 徒單鎰

translations.literal: Tu Danyi
translations.idiomatic: Tu Danyi

sentences.zh: 徒單鎰本名按出，上京路速速保子猛安人。

translations.literal: Tu Danyi; his original name was Anchu. He was a man of Susubao Zimeng'an in Shangjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Danyi, whose birth name was Anchu, came from Susubao Zimeng'an in Shangjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 父烏輦，北京副留守。

translations.literal: His father Wulian was Deputy Military Commissioner of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wulian served as Deputy Military Commissioner of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 鎰穎悟絕倫，甫七歲，習女直字。

translations.literal: Yi was exceptionally quick-witted; at only seven he studied the Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was extraordinarily gifted; by the age of seven he was already learning the Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，詔以女直字譯書籍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dading, an edict ordered books to be translated into Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Dading era, the court decreed that books be translated into Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 五年，翰林侍講學士徒單子溫進所譯《貞觀政要》、《白氏策林》等書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Hanlin Attendant Lecturer Tudan Ziwen presented his translations of the Zhenguan zhengyao, the Bai shi celin, and other works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Hanlin Attendant Lecturer Tudan Ziwen submitted his Jurchen translations of the Essentials of Government in the Zhenguan Reign, Bai Juyi's Policy Forest, and other texts.

sentences.zh: 六年，複進《史記》、《西漢書》，詔頒行之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again presented the Shiji and the Hanshu of the Western Han, and an edict ordered their promulgation.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he presented translations of Records of the Grand Historian and the History of the Western Han as well, and the court ordered them distributed.

sentences.zh: 選諸路學生三十余人，令編修官溫蒂罕締達教以古書，習作詩、策。

translations.literal: More than thirty students from various circuits were selected and ordered to be taught the ancient books by Compiler Wendihan Dida, and to practice composing poetry and policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: Over thirty students from the provinces were chosen; Compiler Wendihan Dida was assigned to teach them the classics and train them in poetry and policy essays.

sentences.zh: 鎰在選中，最精詣，遂通契丹大小字及漢字，該習經史。

translations.literal: Yi was among those selected and was the most accomplished; he thus mastered the large and small Khitan scripts and Chinese characters, and became versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was among the selectees and proved the most accomplished, mastering both the large and small Khitan scripts and Chinese, and gaining a thorough grounding in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 久之，樞密使完顏思敬請教女直人舉進士，下尚書省議。

translations.literal: After some time, Privy Councilor Wanyan Sijin requested that Jurchens be taught to take the jinshi examinations, and the matter was referred to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Privy Councilor Wanyan Sijin proposed instituting jinshi examinations for Jurchens; the proposal was sent to the Ministry of Revenue for discussion.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「初立女直進士科，且免鄉、府兩試，其禮部試、廷試，止對策一道，限字五百以上成。

translations.literal: The memorial said: "When the Jurchen jinshi category is first established, the district and prefectural examinations shall be waived for the time being; for the Ministry of Rites examination and the palace examination, only one policy question shall be required, to be completed in no fewer than five hundred characters."
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read: "At the outset of the Jurchen jinshi track, candidates should be exempt from the district and prefectural rounds; the Ministry of Rites and palace examinations should require only a single policy response of at least five hundred characters."

sentences.zh: 在都設國子學，諸路設府學，並以新進士充教授，士民子弟願學者聽。

translations.literal: A Directorate of Education shall be established in the capital and prefectural schools in each circuit, all staffed with newly minted jinshi as instructors; sons of officials and commoners who wish to study may enroll.
translations.idiomatic: Establish a Directorate of Education in the capital and prefectural schools in each circuit, staffed by recent jinshi as instructors; any official or commoner who wishes to study may enroll.

sentences.zh: 歲久，學者當自眾，即同漢人進士三年一試。

translations.literal: After many years, when students have become numerous, they shall then follow the same triennial examination cycle as Han Chinese jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Once students have grown numerous over the years, Jurchen candidates should follow the same triennial examination schedule as Han jinshi.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月，詔策女直進士，問以求賢為治之道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, an edict ordered a policy examination for Jurchen jinshi candidates on the way of governing through seeking out the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirteenth year, the court held a Jurchen jinshi policy examination on the theme of governing by seeking out worthy men.

sentences.zh: 侍御史完顏蒲涅、太常博士李晏、應奉翰林文字阿不罕德甫、移刺傑、中都路都轉運副使奚釭考試鎰等二十七人及第。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Wanyan Punie, Director of Court Music Li Yan, Hanlin Copyist Abuhan Defu, Yila Jie, and Deputy Transport Commissioner of Zhongdu Circuit Xi Gang examined Yi and twenty-six others, who passed.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Wanyan Punie, Director of Court Music Li Yan, Hanlin Copyist Abuhan Defu, Yila Jie, and Deputy Transport Commissioner of Zhongdu Circuit Xi Gang examined the candidates; Yi and twenty-six others passed.

sentences.zh: 鎰授兩官，餘授一官，上三人為中都路教授，四名以下除各路教授。

translations.literal: Yi was granted two offices; the rest one office each; the top three were appointed instructors of Zhongdu Circuit, and those ranked fourth and below were made instructors in the various circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yi received two appointments; the others one each. The top three became instructors in Zhongdu Circuit, while those ranked fourth and below were assigned as instructors in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔譯諸經，著作佐郎溫蒂罕締達、編修官宗璧、尚書省譯史阿魯、吏部令史楊克忠譯解，翰林修撰移刺傑、應奉翰林文字移刺履講究其義。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict ordered the translation of the classics; Assistant Compiler Wendihan Dida, Compiler Zong Bi, Ministry of Revenue translator Alu, and Ministry of Personnel clerk Yang Kezhong rendered the texts, while Hanlin Academician Yila Jie and Hanlin Copyist Yila Lü expounded their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the court ordered the classics translated. Assistant Compiler Wendihan Dida, Compiler Zong Bi, Ministry translator Alu, and Ministry of Personnel clerk Yang Kezhong produced the renderings, while Hanlin Academician Yila Jie and Hanlin Copyist Yila Lü explained their meaning.

sentences.zh: 鎰自中都路教授選為國子助教。

translations.literal: Yi was selected from his post as instructor of Zhongdu Circuit to become an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was promoted from instructor in Zhongdu Circuit to assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 左丞相紇石烈良弼嘗到學中與鎰談論，深加禮敬。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Heshilie Liangbi once came to the school and conversed with Yi, treating him with deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Heshilie Liangbi once visited the school to talk with Yi and showed him marked respect.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother, he was recalled to serve as compiler at the National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother, he was recalled from retirement to serve as compiler at the National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗問太尉完顏守道曰：「徒單鎰何如人也？

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once asked Grand Marshal Wanyan Shoudao: "What sort of man is Tu Danyi?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong once asked Grand Marshal Wanyan Shoudao, "What manner of man is Tu Danyi?"

sentences.zh: 」守道對曰：「有材力，可任政事。

translations.literal: " Shoudao replied: "He has ability and can be entrusted with government affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao answered, "He has talent and is fit for administrative office."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然，當以劇任處之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So he should; he ought to be placed in a demanding post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Indeed—he should be given a weighty assignment."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「鎰容止溫雅，其心平易。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Yi's bearing is gentle and refined, and his mind is even-tempered."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Yi's manner is gentle and refined, and his disposition is even-tempered."

sentences.zh: 」久之，兼修起居注，累遷翰林待制，兼右司員外郎。

translations.literal: " After some time he was additionally appointed to compile the Veritable Records, and was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman, concurrently serving as Vice Director in the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was also assigned to compile the Veritable Records and rose through successive promotions to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman, concurrently serving as Vice Director in the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 獻《漢光武中興賦》，世宗大悅曰：「不設此科，安得此人。」

translations.literal: He presented a fu-rhapsody on the restoration of the Han under Emperor Guangwu; Shizong was greatly pleased and said: "Had this examination category not been established, how could we have obtained such a man?"
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a rhapsody on Emperor Guangwu's restoration of the Han; Shizong was delighted and said, "Without this examination track, how would we ever have found such a man?"

sentences.zh: 章宗即位，遷左諫議大夫，兼吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong acceded to the throne, Yi was transferred to Left Remonstrance Counselor, concurrently serving as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong came to the throne, Yi was appointed Left Remonstrance Counselor and concurrent Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Mingchang he became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Mingchang era he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 無何，拜參知政事，兼修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, with concurrent duty to compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor, retaining responsibility for compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 鎰言：「人生有欲，不限以制，則侈心無極。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Human life is full of desires; if they are not restrained by regulation, the heart of extravagance knows no limit."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Human beings are driven by desire; without limits imposed by regulation, extravagance knows no bounds."

sentences.zh: 今承平日久，當慎行此道，以為經久之治。

translations.literal: "Now that peace has lasted long, we should carefully follow this path as the foundation of enduring governance."
translations.idiomatic: "Now that peace has endured so long, we must practice restraint carefully if governance is to last."

sentences.zh: 」章宗銳意于治平，鎰上書，其略曰：「臣竊觀唐、虞之書，其臣之進言於君曰'戒哉'，'懋哉'，曰'籲'，曰'都'。

translations.literal: " Zhangzong was keen on achieving order and peace; Yi submitted a memorial, in summary saying: "Your servant has privately observed the books of Tang and Yu: when their ministers addressed the ruler they said 'Be vigilant!' and 'Strive diligently!' and cried 'Alas!' and 'Indeed!'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong was intent on good governance. Yi submitted a memorial that read, in part: "Your servant has studied the records of the sage-kings Yao and Shun. Their ministers addressed the throne with cries of 'Be vigilant!' and 'Strive harder!'—with exclamations of alarm and assent."

sentences.zh: 既陳其戒，複導其美。

translations.literal: Having stated their warnings, they also guided him toward what was excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Having delivered their warnings, they also guided their rulers toward excellence.

sentences.zh: 君之為治也，必曰：'稽於眾，舍己從人'。

translations.literal: In governing, the ruler would invariably say: 'Consult the multitude and set aside one's own views to follow others.'
translations.idiomatic: In governing, the ruler would say, 'Weigh the counsel of the many and set aside private judgment to follow what is right.'

sentences.zh: 既能聽之，又能行之，又從而興起之。

translations.literal: He could not only listen but also act, and further encourage others to rise to the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: He not only listened and acted on counsel but also encouraged others to do the same.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下之間相與如此。

translations.literal: Such was the mutual conduct between ruler and minister, above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the relationship between ruler and minister at every level.

sentences.zh: 陛下繼興隆之運，撫太平之基，誠宜稽古崇德，留意於此，無因物以好惡喜怒，無以好惡喜怒輕忽小善，不恤人言。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has inherited a flourishing fortune and presides over a foundation of peace; you should truly take antiquity as your guide, honor virtue, and attend to this, not letting likes, dislikes, joy, or anger be stirred by external things, and not letting likes, dislikes, joy, or anger cause you to slight small goods or disregard the words of others.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited a flourishing age and presides over an era of peace. You should take antiquity as your guide, honor virtue, and attend to this: do not let passing things stir likes, dislikes, joy, or anger; do not let mood cause you to neglect small goods or disregard counsel from others.

sentences.zh: 夫上下之情有通塞，天地之運有否泰。

translations.literal: For sentiment between above and below may be open or blocked, and the movement of Heaven and Earth may be favorable or adverse.
translations.idiomatic: Communication between ruler and subject may flow freely or be blocked, and the fortunes of Heaven and Earth may turn favorable or adverse.

sentences.zh: 唐陸贄嘗陳隔塞之九弊，上有其六，下有其三。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi of Tang once set forth nine faults of blockage: six pertain to those above, three to those below.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi of the Tang once identified nine faults that block communication between ruler and subject—six belonging to those above, three to those below.

sentences.zh: 陛下能慎其六，為臣子者敢不慎其三哉！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can be careful regarding the six, how dare we as your subjects fail to be careful regarding the three!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty guards against the six faults above, how dare your servants fail to guard against the three below!

sentences.zh: 上下之情既通，則大綱舉而群目張矣。

translations.literal: Once sentiment above and below is open, the great outline is raised and all the lesser threads are drawn taut.
translations.idiomatic: Once communication flows freely between ruler and subject, the great framework is established and every detail falls into place.

sentences.zh: 」進尚書右丞，修史如故。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, continuing to compile history as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat while retaining his duties as historiographer.

sentences.zh: 三年，罷為橫海軍節度使，改定武軍節度使，知平陽府事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was dismissed from office and made Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army, then transferred to Military Commissioner of the Dingwu Army and Administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he left the central government to become Military Commissioner of the Henghai Army, then Military Commissioner of the Dingwu Army and Administrator of Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄭王永蹈判定武軍，鎬王永中判平陽府，相繼得罪，連引者眾，上疑其有黨，或命節度定武，繼又知平陽焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince of Zheng Yong Yongdao had held Dingwu and Prince of Hao Yong Yongzhong had held Pingyang; both successively fell afoul of the law, and many were implicated in their cases. The emperor suspected Yi of factional ties and at times ordered him to command Dingwu, then again to administer Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Zheng had held Dingwu and the Prince of Hao had held Pingyang; both fell from grace in succession, implicating many associates. The emperor suspected Yi of party connections and assigned him first to Dingwu, then to Pingyang—posts previously held by the disgraced princes.

sentences.zh: 改西京留守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Military Governor of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Governor of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，改上京留守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Cheng'an he was transferred to Military Governor of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Cheng'an era he was made Military Governor of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，上問宰臣：「徒單鎰與宗浩孰優？

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor asked the chief ministers: "Who is superior, Tu Danyi or Zong Hao?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor asked his chief ministers, "Which is the better man—Tu Danyi or Zong Hao?"

sentences.zh: 」平章政事張萬公對曰：「皆才能之士，鎰似優者。

translations.literal: " Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong replied: "Both are men of talent; Yi seems the superior."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong answered, "Both are capable men, but Yi appears the stronger."

sentences.zh: 鎰有執守，宗浩多數耳。

translations.literal: Yi has firm principles; Zong Hao is more accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: Yi holds firm to his principles; Zong Hao tends to defer and agree.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何謂多數？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What do you mean by accommodating?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do you mean by deferring and agreeing?"

sentences.zh: 」萬公曰：「宗浩微似趨合。

translations.literal: " Wangong said: "Zong Hao slightly tends toward currying favor."
translations.idiomatic: Wangong said, "Zong Hao leans a little toward telling the emperor what he wants to hear."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，鎰拜平章政事，封濟國公。

translations.literal: " Before long Yi was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yi was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 淑妃李氏擅寵，兄弟恣橫，朝臣往往出入其門。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort Li monopolized the emperor's favor; her brothers acted with reckless license, and court officials often passed in and out of their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort Li held exclusive sway over the emperor's affection; her brothers acted with impunity, and court officials routinely sought them out.

sentences.zh: 是時烈風昏噎連日，詔問變異之由。

translations.literal: At that time fierce winds and murky choking air persisted for days on end; an edict inquired into the cause of these anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Violent winds and choking murk hung over the capital for days; the court issued an edict asking what omens these disturbances signified.

sentences.zh: 鎰上疏略曰：「仁、義、禮、智、信謂之五常，父義、母慈、兄友、弟敬、子孝謂之五德。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial in summary saying: "Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are called the Five Constants; a father's righteousness, a mother's kindness, an elder brother's friendliness, a younger brother's respect, and a son's filial piety are called the Five Virtues."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial that read, in part: "Benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and trustworthiness are the Five Constants; a father's righteousness, a mother's kindness, an elder brother's friendship, a younger brother's respect, and a son's filial piety are the Five Virtues."

sentences.zh: 今五常不立，五德不興，縉紳學古之士棄禮義，忘廉恥，細民違道畔義，迷不知返，背毀天常，骨內相殘，動傷和氣，此非一朝一夕之故也。

translations.literal: Now the Five Constants are not established and the Five Virtues do not flourish; gentry scholars who study antiquity abandon propriety and righteousness and forget integrity and shame; common people violate the Way and turn against righteousness, lost without knowing how to return, turning their backs on Heaven's constants and tearing at one another within the bone and flesh, constantly harming harmonious qi—this is not the work of a day or a night.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Five Constants lie in ruins and the Five Virtues have withered. Scholar-officials who study the classics abandon propriety and forget shame; common people stray from the Way and turn against righteousness, lost without knowing how to return. They violate Heaven's order, tear at one another like flesh against bone, and constantly disrupt the harmonious qi of the realm. This did not happen overnight.

sentences.zh: 今宜正薄俗，順人心，父父子子夫夫婦婦，各得其道，然後和氣普洽，福祿薦臻矣。

translations.literal: Now we should rectify shallow customs, accord with the people's hearts, let fathers be fathers and sons sons, husbands husbands and wives wives, each in his proper place—then harmonious qi will pervade everywhere and blessings and emoluments will arrive in succession.
translations.idiomatic: We must now correct shallow customs and align with the people's hearts—let every father be a father, every son a son, every husband a husband, every wife a wife, each in his proper place. Only then will harmonious qi spread throughout the realm and blessings follow in abundance.

sentences.zh: 」因論：「為政之術，其急有二。

translations.literal: " He went on to discuss: "In the art of governing, two matters are most urgent."
translations.idiomatic: He continued: "In the art of governance, two matters demand immediate attention."

sentences.zh: 一曰正臣下之心。

translations.literal: The first is to rectify the hearts of officials.
translations.idiomatic: First, rectify the hearts of officials.

sentences.zh: 竊見群下不明禮義，趨利者眾，何以責小民之從化哉。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that those below do not understand propriety and righteousness, and that many rush after profit—how can we demand that common people follow the transforming influence?
translations.idiomatic: I observe that officials below do not understand propriety and righteousness, and that many rush after profit. How can we expect common people to follow their example?

sentences.zh: 其用人也，德器為上，才美為下，兼之者待以不次，才下行美者次之，雖有才能，行義無取者，抑而下之，則臣下之趨向正矣。

translations.literal: In employing men, moral character and capacity should rank highest, talent and excellence lowest; those who combine both should be treated with extraordinary promotion; those with talent below but conduct above should rank next; even if they have ability, those whose conduct and righteousness are not acceptable should be demoted—then the orientation of officials will be correct.
translations.idiomatic: In appointing men, moral character and capacity should rank highest, talent alone lowest. Those who combine both deserve exceptional promotion; those with lesser talent but sterling conduct come next. Even men of ability should be demoted if their conduct is unworthy. Then officials will know which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 其二曰導學者之志。

translations.literal: The second is to guide the aspirations of students.
translations.idiomatic: Second, guide the aspirations of students.

sentences.zh: 教化之行，興於學校。

translations.literal: The spread of transforming instruction arises from the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming instruction spreads from the schools.

sentences.zh: 今學者失其本真，經史雅奧，委而不習，藻飾虛詞，釣取祿利，乞令取士兼問經史故實，使學者皆守經學，不惑于近習之靡，則善矣。

translations.literal: Now students have lost their original substance; the classics and histories, profound and recondite, they set aside and do not study, instead ornamenting empty phrases to fish for salary and profit. I beg that in selecting scholars the examinations also test knowledge of facts from the classics and histories, so that students all hold to classical learning and are not misled by the dissipation of recent fashions—then it would be well.
translations.idiomatic: Students today have lost their grounding. They neglect the profound classics and histories in favor of ornamented empty phrases designed to win office and salary. I beg that civil examinations also test knowledge of facts from the classics and histories, so that students hold to genuine learning and are not seduced by fashionable superficiality.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「凡天下之事，叢來者非一端，形似者非一體，法制不能盡，隱於近似，乃生異論。

translations.literal: " He also said: "All affairs under Heaven come in clusters from more than one source; what appears similar is not of one form; regulations and laws cannot cover everything; what is hidden in near resemblance gives rise to divergent opinions."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Affairs under Heaven rarely spring from a single cause; what looks alike is not always the same thing. Law and regulation cannot cover every case; when matters resemble one another only superficially, divergent opinions arise."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：'義者天下之制也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Righteousness is the standard of all under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Righteousness is the standard of all under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: '《記》曰：'義為斷之節。

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Righteousness is the measure for deciding.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says, 'Righteousness is the measure by which decisions are made.'

sentences.zh: '伏望陛下臨制萬機，事有異議，少凝聖慮，尋繹其端，則裁斷有定，而疑可辨矣。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty, in presiding over the myriad affairs of state, when matters give rise to dispute, will pause briefly to concentrate your sacred attention, trace matters to their beginnings—then judgments will have a fixed basis and doubts can be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty, when presiding over the myriad affairs of state and disputes arise, to pause and trace each matter to its root. Then your judgments will have a firm basis and doubts can be resolved.

sentences.zh: 」鎰言皆切時弊，上雖納其說，而不能行。

translations.literal: " All of Yi's words cut to the timely abuses; although the emperor accepted his views, he could not put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's counsel addressed the abuses of the day directly. The emperor accepted his reasoning but could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 上問漢高帝、光武優劣。

translations.literal: The emperor asked about the relative merits of Emperor Gaozu of Han and Emperor Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked which was the greater ruler—Emperor Gaozu of Han or Emperor Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 平章政事張萬公對曰：「高祖優甚。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong replied: "Gaozu is far superior."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong answered, "Gaozu was by far the greater."

sentences.zh: 」鎰曰：「光武再造漢業，在位三十年，無沈湎冒色之事。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "Guangwu restored the Han enterprise; during thirty years on the throne he had no affairs of dissipation or reckless pursuit of beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Guangwu restored the Han dynasty and reigned thirty years without a single episode of dissipation or reckless pursuit of women."

sentences.zh: 高祖惑戚姬，卒至於亂。

translations.literal: Gaozu was beguiled by Consort Qi and in the end came to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was beguiled by Consort Qi and brought the realm to disorder.

sentences.zh: 由是言之，光武優。

translations.literal: Spoken from this perspective, Guangwu is superior.
translations.idiomatic: By that measure, Guangwu was the greater ruler.

sentences.zh: 」上默然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 鎰蓋以元妃李氏隆寵過盛，故微諫雲。

translations.literal: Yi presumably offered this subtle remonstrance because Primary Consort Li's extravagant favor was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was offering an oblique remonstrance against the excessive favor shown Primary Consort Li.

sentences.zh: 泰和四年，罷知咸平府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was dismissed from administering Xianping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Taihe era he was relieved of his post as Administrator of Xianping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，改南京留守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Military Governor of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Military Governor of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙知河中府，兼陝西安撫使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to administer Hezhong Prefecture, concurrently serving as Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Administrator of Hezhong Prefecture and concurrent Pacification Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 僕散揆行省河南、陝西，元帥府雖受揆節制，實顓方面，上思用謀臣制之，由是升宣撫使一品，鎰改知京兆府事，充宣撫使，陝西元帥府並受節制。

translations.literal: Pusan Kui held the regional command of Henan and Shaanxi; although the Marshal's Headquarters was subject to Kui's regulation, in fact it monopolized its region. The emperor thought to use a strategist to restrain it; thereby the Pacification Commissioner was raised to first rank, Yi was changed to Administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture and appointed Pacification Commissioner, and the Shaanxi Marshal's Headquarters all came under his regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Kui held regional command over Henan and Shaanxi. Although the Marshal's Headquarters nominally answered to Kui, in practice it dominated the region. The emperor decided to place a strategist in charge; the Pacification Commissioner was elevated to first rank, Yi was made Administrator of Jingzhao Prefecture and Pacification Commissioner, and the Shaanxi Marshal's Headquarters was placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「將帥雖武悍，久曆行陣，而宋人狡獪，亦資算勝。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Although commanders are fierce in war and long experienced in the ranks, the Song people are crafty and cunning, and victory also depends on stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Commanders may be fierce warriors long seasoned in battle, but the Song are crafty opponents, and victory also depends on strategy."

sentences.zh: 卿之智略，朕所深悉，且股肱舊臣，故有此寄。

translations.literal: Your stratagems and plans Your Majesty deeply understands, and moreover as an old minister of the inner circle, you are therefore entrusted with this charge.
translations.idiomatic: Your strategic mind is well known to us, and as a trusted veteran of the inner circle, you are entrusted with this responsibility.

sentences.zh: 宜以長刺禦敵，厲兵撫民，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: You should use long-range thrusts to repel the enemy, sharpen the troops and comfort the people, in accord with Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Press the enemy at long range, keep the army sharp, and care for the people—that is Our wish.

sentences.zh: 」鎰言：「初置急遞鋪，本為轉送文牒，今一切乘驛，非便。

translations.literal: " Yi said: "When the urgent relay stations were first established, it was originally to forward documents; now everyone rides the post horses for every purpose, which is not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The urgent relay stations were established to forward official documents. Now everyone uses the post horses for private travel, which defeats their purpose."

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 始置提控急遞鋪官。

translations.literal: Supervisory officials for the urgent relay stations were first established.
translations.idiomatic: The court established supervisory officials for the urgent relay stations.

sentences.zh: 自中都至真定、平陽置者，達於京兆。

translations.literal: Those established from the Central Capital to Zhending and Pingyang reached Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Stations from the Central Capital through Zhending and Pingyang connected to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 京兆至鳳翔置者，達於臨洮。

translations.literal: Those established from Jingzhao to Fengxiang reached Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Stations from Jingzhao through Fengxiang connected to Lintao.

sentences.zh: 自真定至彰德置者，達于南京。

translations.literal: Those established from Zhending to Zhangde reached the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Stations from Zhending through Zhangde connected to the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 自南京分至歸德置者，達於泗州、壽州，分至許州置者，達于鄧州。

translations.literal: Those branching from the Southern Capital to Guide reached Sizhou and Shouzhou; those branching to Xuzhou reached Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Branches from the Southern Capital through Guide reached Sizhou and Shouzhou; a branch through Xuzhou reached Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 自中都至滄州置者，達於益都府。

translations.literal: Those established from the Central Capital to Cangzhou reached Yidu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Stations from the Central Capital through Cangzhou connected to Yidu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自此郵達無複滯焉。

translations.literal: From this time forward postal delivery was no longer delayed.
translations.idiomatic: From that point onward the relay system no longer suffered delays.

sentences.zh: 七年，吳曦死，宋安丙分兵出秦、隴間。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Wu Xi died; Song An Bing divided his troops and advanced from the Qin and Long regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Wu Xi died, and Song An Bing divided his forces and advanced from the Qin and Long frontier.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔鎰出兵金、房以分掣宋人梁、益、漢、沔兵勢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered Yi to send troops from Jin and Fang to divide and restrain the Song forces in Liang, Yi, Han, and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court ordered Yi to deploy troops from Jin and Fang to draw off Song forces massed in Liang, Yi, Han, and Mian.

sentences.zh: 鎰遣行軍都統斡勒葉祿瓦、副統把回海、完顏摑刺以步騎五千出商州。

translations.literal: Yi dispatched Campaign Commander-in-Chief Wolie Yelüwa, Vice Commander Ba Huihai, and Wanyan Guaci with five thousand infantry and cavalry out of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Campaign Commander-in-Chief Wolie Yelüwa, Vice Commander Ba Huihai, and Wanyan Guaci with five thousand foot and horse soldiers out of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，葉祿瓦拔鶻嶺關，摑刺別將攻破燕子關新道口，回海取小湖關敖倉，至營口鎮，破宋兵千餘人，追至上津縣，斬首八百餘級，遂取上津縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Yelüwa captured Hegu Pass; Guaci as detached commander stormed the new road at Yanzi Pass; Huihai took Xiaohu Pass Aocang, reached Yingkou Town, defeated more than a thousand Song troops, pursued to Shangjin County, beheaded more than eight hundred, and then captured Shangjin County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Yelüwa took Hegu Pass. Guaci's detached force broke through the new road at Yanzi Pass. Huihai seized Xiaohu Pass and Aocang, advanced to Yingkou Town, routed over a thousand Song troops, pursued them to Shangjin County, took more than eight hundred heads, and captured the county.

sentences.zh: 葉祿瓦破宋兵二千于平溪，將趨金州。

translations.literal: Yelüwa defeated two thousand Song troops at Pingxi and was about to advance on Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yelüwa routed two thousand Song troops at Pingxi and prepared to march on Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋王柟以書乞和，詔鎰召葉祿瓦軍退守鶻嶺關。

translations.literal: Song Wang Kan sent a letter begging for peace; an edict ordered Yi to recall Yelüwa's army to hold Hegu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Song commander Wang Kan sent a letter suing for peace; the court ordered Yi to recall Yelüwa's army to defend Hegu Pass.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，宋安丙遣景統領由梅子溪、新道口、硃砂穀襲鶻嶺關，回海，摑刺擊走之，斬景統領於陣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year Song An Bing dispatched Jing Tongling by way of Meizi Stream, Xindao Pass, and Zhusha Valley to attack Hegu Pass; Huihai and Guaci drove them off and beheaded Jing Tongling on the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year Song An Bing sent Jing Tongling against Hegu Pass by way of Meizi Stream, Xindao Pass, and Zhusha Valley. Huihai and Guaci repulsed the attack and killed Jing Tongling in battle.

sentences.zh: 是歲，罷兵。

translations.literal: That year hostilities ceased.
translations.idiomatic: That year the armies stood down.

sentences.zh: 鎰遷特進，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: Yi was transferred to Special Advancement and granted rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was promoted to Special Advancement and received gifts of varying value.

sentences.zh: 改知真定府事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Zhending Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Administrator of Zhending Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大安初，加儀同三司，封濮國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Da'an he was given the additional title of Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Da'an era he was granted the rank of Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Pu.

sentences.zh: 改東京留守，過闕入見。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and, passing through the capital, entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Military Governor of the Eastern Capital and, on passing through the capital, was granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王謂鎰曰：「卿兩朝舊德，欲用卿為相。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Shao said to Yi: "You are a veteran of merit from two reigns; I wish to employ you as chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Shao told Yi, "You have served two reigns with distinction. I wish to make you chancellor."

sentences.zh: 太尉匡，卿之門人，朕不可屈卿下之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Kuang is your disciple; I cannot demean you by placing you beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Kuang is your former student. I cannot place you beneath him.

sentences.zh: 」遷開府儀同三司，佩金符，充遼東安撫副使。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Grand Master with Gold Seal and Jade Ribbon, wore the gold tally, and served as Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was made Grand Master with Gold Seal and Jade Ribbon, given the gold tally, and appointed Deputy Pacification Commissioner of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 三年，改上京留守。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Military Governor of the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Military Governor of the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 平章政事獨吉思忠敗績於會河堡，中都戒嚴，鎰曰：「事急矣。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong suffered defeat at Huihe Fort; the Central Capital was placed under martial law. Yi said: "The situation is urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong was defeated at Huihe Fort, and the Central Capital went on alert. Yi said, "The situation is critical."

sentences.zh: 」乃選兵二萬，遣同知烏古孫兀屯將之，入衛中都。

translations.literal: " He then selected twenty thousand troops and dispatched Vice Commissioner Wugusun Wutun to command them to enter and defend the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He selected twenty thousand troops and sent Vice Commissioner Wugusun Wutun to lead them in defense of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，征拜尚書右丞相，監修國史。

translations.literal: The court commended this and summoned him to appointment as Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his initiative and summoned him to serve as Right Chancellor of the Secretariat, with responsibility for compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 鎰言：「自用兵以來，彼聚而行，我散而守，以聚攻散，其敗必然。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Since the beginning of the war they have massed to advance while we have dispersed to defend; attacking the dispersed with the massed, defeat is inevitable."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Since the war began the enemy has massed to strike while we have scattered to defend. Concentrated force against dispersed garrisons must end in defeat."

sentences.zh: 不若入保大城，並力備禦。

translations.literal: It would be better to withdraw into the great walled cities and combine strength for defense.
translations.idiomatic: We should withdraw into the great walled cities and concentrate our strength for defense.

sentences.zh: 昌、桓、撫三州素號富實，人皆勇健，可以內徙，益我兵勢，人畜貨財，不至亡失。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Chang, Huan, and Fu have long been known as rich and substantial; their people are all brave and strong and can be moved inward to augment our military strength, so that people, livestock, goods, and wealth will not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Chang, Huan, and Fu are famously prosperous, and their people are brave and hardy. Relocate them inward to strengthen our armies and preserve our people, livestock, and wealth.

sentences.zh: 」平章政事移刺、參知政事梁絪曰：「如此是自蹙境土也。

translations.literal: " Grand Councilor Yila and Vice Grand Councilor Liang Yin said: "To do so is to constrict our own territory."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yila and Vice Grand Councilor Liang Yin objected, "That would only shrink our own territory."

sentences.zh: 」衛紹王以責鎰。

translations.literal: " Prince of Wei Shao reproached Yi for it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Shao rebuked Yi.

sentences.zh: 鎰複奏曰：「遼東國家根本，距中都數千里，萬一受兵，州府顧望，必須報可，誤事多矣。

translations.literal: Yi again memorialized: "Liaodong is the fundamental root of the state; it is several thousand li from the Central Capital. If it should come under attack, the prefectures and districts will look about in hesitation and must await approval—many affairs will be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted another memorial: "Liaodong is the foundation of the state, yet it lies thousands of li from the Central Capital. If it comes under attack, local officials will hesitate while awaiting approval from the capital, and precious time will be lost."

sentences.zh: 可遣大臣行省以鎮之。

translations.literal: A great minister can be dispatched with regional command to stabilize it.
translations.idiomatic: Send a senior minister with regional command to secure the region.

sentences.zh: 」衛紹王不悅曰：「無故置行省，徒搖人心耳。

translations.literal: " Prince of Wei Shao said displeased: "To establish regional command without cause only shakes the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Shao said irritably, "Creating a regional command post for no reason will only unsettle the people."

sentences.zh: 」其後失昌、桓、撫三州，衛紹王乃大悔曰：「從丞相之言，當不至此！

translations.literal: " Later, when Chang, Huan, and Fu were lost, Prince of Wei Shao greatly regretted it and said: "Had I followed the Chancellor's words, it would not have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chang, Huan, and Fu were lost, Prince of Wei Shao bitterly regretted his decision. "Had I listened to the Chancellor," he said, "it would never have come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」頃之，東京不守，衛紹王自訟曰：「我見丞相恥哉！」

translations.literal: " Before long the Eastern Capital could not be held; Prince of Wei Shao blamed himself and said: "How ashamed I am to face the Chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Eastern Capital fell. Prince of Wei Shao reproached himself: "How can I face the Chancellor without shame!"

sentences.zh: 術虎高琪駐兵縉山，甚得人心，士樂為用。

translations.literal: Shuhu Gaoqi stationed troops at Jin Mountain and won great popular support; soldiers were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhu Gaoqi held Jin Mountain with his troops and won the people's hearts; his soldiers served him gladly.

sentences.zh: 至甯元年，尚書左丞完顏綱將行省於縉山，鎰謂綱曰：「行省不必自往，不若益兵為便。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyong, Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Wanyan Gang was about to take regional command at Jin Mountain. Yi said to Gang: "The regional commander need not go in person; it would be better simply to reinforce the troops."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyong, Left Vice Minister Wanyan Gang prepared to take regional command at Jin Mountain. Yi told him, "You need not go yourself. Reinforcing Gaoqi's troops would serve better."

sentences.zh: 」綱不聽，且行，鎰遣人止之曰：「高琪之功，即行省之功也。

translations.literal: " Gang would not listen and set out. Yi sent someone to stop him, saying: "Gaoqi's achievement is the regional commander's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Gang refused to listen and set out. Yi sent a messenger after him: "Gaoqi's victory will be your victory."

sentences.zh: 」亦不聽。

translations.literal: " He still would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gang would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 綱至縉山，遂敗績焉。

translations.literal: When Gang reached Jin Mountain he suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Gang reached Jin Mountain and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 頃之，鎰墜馬傷足在告，聞胡沙虎難作，命駕將入省。

translations.literal: Before long Yi fell from his horse and injured his foot; while on leave he heard that Hu Shahu's disturbance had broken out and ordered his carriage to enter the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yi fell from his horse and injured his foot. While on sick leave he heard that Hu Shahu had launched a coup and ordered his carriage to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 或告之曰：「省府相幕皆以軍士守之，不可入矣。

translations.literal: Someone told him: "The offices of the Secretariat and ministries are all guarded by soldiers; you cannot enter."
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him, "Soldiers now guard every office of the Secretariat and ministries. You cannot enter."

sentences.zh: 」少頃，兵士索人于閭巷，鎰乃還第。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward soldiers were seizing people in the lanes; Yi then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long soldiers were dragging people from the streets. Yi returned home.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎意不可測，方猶豫，不能自定，乃詣鎰問疾，從人望也。

translations.literal: Hu Shahu's intentions could not be gauged; he was hesitating and could not decide for himself, and so came to inquire after Yi's illness, following the people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu's intentions were uncertain; he hesitated, unable to decide his course, and came to inquire after Yi's health as the people expected.

sentences.zh: 鎰從容謂之曰：「翼王，章宗之兄，顯宗長子，眾望所屬，元帥決策立之，萬世之功也。

translations.literal: Yi calmly said to him: "Prince of Yi, elder brother of Zhangzong and eldest son of Xianzong, is where popular expectation lies. If the Marshal decides to install him, it will be an achievement for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said calmly, "Prince of Yi is Zhangzong's elder brother and Xianzong's eldest son—the man the people expect. If you install him, Marshal, you will earn eternal glory."

sentences.zh: 」胡沙虎默然而去，乃迎宣宗於彰德。

translations.literal: " Hu Shahu departed in silence and then went to welcome Emperor Xuanzong at Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu left without a word and went to welcome Emperor Xuanzong at Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 胡沙虎既殺徒單南平，欲執其弟知真定府事銘，鎰說之曰：「車駕道出真定，鎬王家在威州，河北人心易搖，徒單銘有變，朝廷危矣。

translations.literal: After Hu Shahu had killed Tudan Nanping, he wished to seize his younger brother Ming, Administrator of Zhending Prefecture. Yi persuaded him: "The imperial carriage will pass through Zhending; the Prince of Hao's household is at Weizhou; hearts in Hebei are easily shaken—if Tudan Ming rebels, the court will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: After killing Tudan Nanping, Hu Shahu planned to arrest his brother Ming, Administrator of Zhending. Yi persuaded him, "The imperial procession will pass through Zhending. The Prince of Hao's household is at Weizhou, and hearts in Hebei are easily unsettled. If Tudan Ming turns against us, the court will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 不如與之金牌，奉迎車駕，銘必感元帥之恩。

translations.literal: It would be better to give him a gold tally and have him welcome the imperial carriage; Ming will surely be moved by the Marshal's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Give him a gold tally and charge him with welcoming the imperial procession. Ming will be bound to you by gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」胡沙虎從之。

translations.literal: " Hu Shahu followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shahu took his advice.

sentences.zh: 至寧、貞祐之際，轉敗為功，惟鎰是賴焉。

translations.literal: At the juncture of Zhiyong and Zhenyou, in turning defeat into victory, the court relied on Yi alone.
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis of the Zhiyong and Zhenyou eras, when defeat had to be turned to victory, the court depended on Yi alone.

sentences.zh: 鎰明敏方正，學問該貫，一時名士，皆出其門，多至卿相。

translations.literal: Yi was bright, perceptive, upright, and square; his learning was comprehensive; the eminent scholars of the age all came from his gate, many rising to ministerial rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was brilliant, upright, and learned to the full breadth of the classics. The leading scholars of his day studied under him, and many rose to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗歎文士委頓，雖巧拙不同，要以仁義道德為本，乃著《學之急》、《道之要》二篇。

translations.literal: He once lamented that literary men were enervated; though skill and clumsiness differ, benevolence, righteousness, and moral virtue should be the foundation, and he therefore composed two essays, "The Urgency of Learning" and "The Essentials of the Way."
translations.idiomatic: He once lamented that literati had grown slack. Skill might vary, but benevolence and moral virtue must remain the foundation. He wrote two essays, "The Urgency of Learning" and "The Essentials of the Way."

sentences.zh: 太學諸生刻之于石。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial Academy had them carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial Academy had them carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 有《弘道集》六卷。

translations.literal: He had a Hongdao ji in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a six-scroll collection entitled Hongdao ji (Expanding the Way).

sentences.zh: 賈鉉，字鼎臣，博州博平人。

translations.literal: Jia Xuan, style name Dingchen, was a native of Boping in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuan, style name Dingchen, came from Boping in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 性純厚，好學問。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and substantial, and he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure-hearted and studious by nature.

sentences.zh: 中大定十三年進士，調滕州軍事判官、單州司候，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Dading, was assigned as Military Adjutant of Tengzhou and Registrar of Danzhou, and was appointed clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirteenth year of Dading, served as Military Adjutant of Tengzhou and Registrar of Danzhou, and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 章宗為右丞相，深器重之，除陝西東路轉運副使。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong was Right Chancellor he deeply valued him and appointed him Deputy Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhangzong was Right Chancellor he held Xuan in high regard and appointed him Deputy Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部主事，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a principal official of the Ministry of Justice and was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a principal official in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，改右司諫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant Censor and transferred to Remonstrance Counselor in the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Censor and then Remonstrance Counselor in the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上疏論邊戍利害，上嘉納之，遷左諫議大夫兼工部侍郎，與党懷英同刊修《遼史》。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing the advantages and disadvantages of frontier garrisons; the emperor commended and accepted it. He was promoted to Left Remonstrance Counselor, concurrently Vice Minister of Works, and together with Dang Huaiying revised the Liaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the strengths and weaknesses of frontier garrisons; the emperor praised and adopted his recommendations. He was made Left Remonstrance Counselor and concurrent Vice Minister of Works, and joined Dang Huaiying in compiling the History of Liao.

sentences.zh: 鉉上書曰：「親民之官，任情立威，所用決杖，分徑長短不如法式，甚者以鐵刃置於杖端，因而致死。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial saying: "Officials close to the people, acting on whim to establish authority, use the beating staff with diameters and lengths not conforming to statute; in extreme cases they place iron blades at the end of the staff, thereby causing death."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a memorial: "Local magistrates, seeking to assert authority at will, use beating staffs whose dimensions do not conform to statute. In the worst cases they fix iron blades to the ends of the staffs and kill their victims."

sentences.zh: 間者陰陽愆戾，和氣不通，未必不由此也。

translations.literal: Recently yin and yang have been out of harmony and harmonious qi does not flow—this may not be unrelated.
translations.idiomatic: Recently yin and yang have fallen out of balance and harmonious qi has been disrupted—this may well be one cause.

sentences.zh: 願下州郡申明舊章，檢量封記，按察官其檢察不如法者，具以名聞。

translations.literal: I beg that the prefectures and districts be ordered to clarify the old regulations, inspect and seal the staffs, and that surveillance officials investigate those not conforming to law and report their names.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that prefectures be ordered to enforce the old regulations, inspect and seal all beating staffs, and that surveillance officials report by name any magistrate who violates the law.

sentences.zh: 內庭敕斷，亦依已定程式。

translations.literal: Imperial commands and judgments within the palace should also follow the established procedures.
translations.idiomatic: Palace punishments should likewise follow established procedures.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: " The decree was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 複上書論山東採茶事，其大概以為「茶樹隨山皆有，一切護邏，已奪民利，因而以揀茶樹執誣小民，嚇取貨賂，宜嚴禁止。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial on the tea-picking affairs of Shandong, in general holding that "tea trees grow on every mountain; guarding them all along the routes has already seized the people's profit, and on this pretext they seize and falsely accuse common people over selecting tea trees and extort bribes—this should be strictly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial on tea collection in Shandong, arguing that "tea trees grow on every hillside. Guarding them all has already robbed the people of their livelihood, and officials use the pretense of inspecting tea trees to frame commoners and extort bribes. This practice must be strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 仍令按察司約束。

translations.literal: The surveillance commission should still be ordered to restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commission should be ordered to enforce the ban.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，遷禮部尚書，諫議如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was transferred to Minister of Rites, retaining his remonstrance duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was made Minister of Rites while retaining his remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 是時有詔，凡奉敕商量照勘公事皆期日聞奏。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict that all official business discussed and investigated by imperial command must be reported by a set date.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that all official business conducted by imperial command be reported by a fixed deadline.

sentences.zh: 鉉言：「若如此，恐官吏迫于限期，姑務苟簡，反害事體。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "If it is thus, I fear officials, pressed by the deadline, will for the moment pursue what is hasty and simple, to the harm of the substance of affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan objected: "If this rule stands, officials pressed by deadlines will settle for hasty, superficial work, to the detriment of sound governance."

sentences.zh: 況簿書自有常程，御史台治其稽緩，如事有應密，三月未絕者，令具次第以聞。

translations.literal: Moreover documents have their regular procedures, and the Censorate punishes delay; if affairs requiring secrecy are not concluded within three months, let the sequence be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Documents already follow regular procedures, and the Censorate punishes delay. For confidential matters still unresolved after three months, officials should report progress in sequence.

sentences.zh: 下尚書省議。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was sent to the Ministry of Revenue for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 如省部可即定奪者，須三月擬奏，如取會案牘卒難補勘者，先具次第奏知，更限一月結絕，違者准稽緩制書罪之。」

translations.literal: If the ministries can decide immediately, a draft memorial must be prepared within three months; if gathering documents makes supplementary investigation difficult to complete, first report the sequence to inform, with a further limit of one month for conclusion; violators shall be punished according to the statute on delay.
translations.idiomatic: Matters the ministries can decide immediately should be memorialized within three months. Cases requiring cross-reference of documents that cannot be completed promptly should be reported in sequence first, with one additional month allowed for conclusion. Violators should be punished under the statute on delay.

sentences.zh: 上議置相，欲用鉉，宰臣薦孫即康。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed appointing a chancellor and wished to use Xuan; the chief ministers recommended Sun Jikang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor discussed appointing a chancellor, he wished to use Xuan, but the chief ministers recommended Sun Jikang.

sentences.zh: 張萬公曰：「即康及第在鉉前。

translations.literal: Zhang Wangong said: "Jikang passed the examination before Xuan."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wangong said, "Jikang passed the examinations before Xuan."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「用相安問榜次？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In appointing a chancellor, why ask about examination ranking?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When appointing a chancellor, who cares about examination ranking?"

sentences.zh: 朕意以為賈鉉才可用也。

translations.literal: In my mind Jia Xuan's talent can be employed.
translations.idiomatic: In my view Jia Xuan's talents are the ones we need.

sentences.zh: 」然竟用即康焉。

translations.literal: " Yet in the end Jikang was used.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Sun Jikang was appointed.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，禦試，鉉為監試官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, at the imperial examination, Xuan was supervising examiner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, at the palace examination, Xuan served as supervising examiner.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「丞相宗浩嘗言試題頗易，由是進士例不讀書。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Chancellor Zong Hao once said the examination topics were rather easy, and from this jinshi routinely did not study."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Chancellor Zong Hao once complained that examination topics were too easy, and jinshi candidates have stopped studying as a result."

sentences.zh: 朕今以《日合天統》為賦題。

translations.literal: I now take "The Sun Conforms to Heaven's Principle" as the fu topic.
translations.idiomatic: I have set "The Sun Conforms to Heaven's Principle" as this year's fu topic.

sentences.zh: 」鉉曰：「題則佳矣，恐非所以牢籠天下士也。

translations.literal: " Xuan said: "The topic is excellent, but I fear it is not the means to encompass the scholars of all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said, "The topic is excellent, but I fear it is not the way to draw out the best scholars in the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「帝王以難題窘舉人，固不可，欲使自今積致學業而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "For an emperor to use difficult topics to embarrass candidates is certainly not permissible; I only wish that from now on they will accumulate and achieve learning."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "An emperor should not use difficult topics merely to embarrass candidates. I only want them to apply themselves to learning from now on."

sentences.zh: 」遂用之。

translations.literal: " The topic was then used.
translations.idiomatic: The topic stood.

sentences.zh: 久之，鉉與審官院掌書大中漏言除授事。

translations.literal: After some time Xuan, together with Dazhong, clerk of the Court of Review, leaked word of appointment matters.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later Xuan and Dazhong, a clerk of the Court of Review, leaked word of pending appointments.

sentences.zh: 上謂鉉曰：「卿罪自知之矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xuan: "You know your own offense."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Xuan, "You know your own offense."

sentences.zh: 然卿久參機務，補益弘多，不深罪也。

translations.literal: Yet you have long participated in state affairs and your contributions have been many and great; you will not be deeply punished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have long served at the center of government and contributed greatly. I will not punish you severely.

sentences.zh: 」乃出為安武軍節度使，改知濟南府。

translations.literal: " He was then sent out as Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army and transferred to administer Jinan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Anwu Army and then Administrator of Jinan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 致仕。

translations.literal: He retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired from office.

sentences.zh: 貞祐元年薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhenyou.

sentences.zh: 承安元年，遷左諫議大夫，改河東南路轉運使，召為中都路都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Cheng'an he was transferred to Left Remonstrance Counselor, then to Transport Commissioner of Hedong South Circuit, and summoned as Chief Transport Commissioner of Zhongdu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Cheng'an he was made Left Remonstrance Counselor, then Transport Commissioner of Hedong South Circuit, and finally summoned as Chief Transport Commissioner of Zhongdu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 初置講議錢谷官十人，鐸為選首。

translations.literal: When the ten Discuss-and-Review officials for revenue and grain were first established, Duo was chosen as their head.
translations.idiomatic: When the ten Discuss-and-Review officials for fiscal affairs were first established, Duo was chosen to lead them.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Cheng'an he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鐸因轉對奏曰：「比年號令，或已行而中輟，或既改而複行，更張太煩，百姓不信。

translations.literal: Duo, taking his turn to address the throne, memorialized: "In recent years edicts have sometimes been promulgated and then halted midway, or changed and then reissued; alterations are too frequent and the people do not trust them."
translations.idiomatic: Addressing the throne in rotation, Duo said, "In recent years edicts have been issued and then halted, or revised and reissued. The constant changes have left the people distrustful of government."

sentences.zh: 乞自今凡將下令，再三講究，如有益於治則必行，無恤小民之言。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on, whenever an order is about to be issued, it be deliberated again and again; if it benefits governance it must be carried out, without regard for the words of petty people.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that hereafter every proposed edict be thoroughly deliberated. If it truly benefits governance, enforce it without heeding petty complaints.

sentences.zh: 」國子司業紇石烈善才亦言：「頒行法令，絲綸既出，尤當固守。

translations.literal: " Guozi Vice Director Heshilie Shancai also said: "When laws and orders are promulgated, once the imperial rescript has gone forth it should especially be firmly upheld."
translations.idiomatic: Guozi Vice Director Heshilie Shancai added, "Once an edict has been promulgated, it must be upheld steadfastly."

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年閏十二月，上召鐸、戶部侍郎張複亨議交鈔。

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the second year of Taihe the emperor summoned Duo and Vice Minister of Revenue Zhang Fuheng to discuss exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month of the second year of Taihe the emperor summoned Duo and Vice Minister Zhang Fuheng to discuss paper currency.

sentences.zh: 複亨曰：「三合同鈔可行。

translations.literal: Fuheng said: "The Three-Circuit Joint Exchange Note can be implemented."
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng said, "The Three-Circuit Joint Exchange Note can be adopted."

sentences.zh: 」鐸請廢不用，詰難久之，複亨議詘。

translations.literal: " Duo requested that it be abolished and not used; he argued back and forth for a long time until Fuheng's proposal was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Duo argued for abolishing it entirely. After prolonged debate Fuheng's proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂侍臣曰：「孫鐸剛正人也，雖古魏徵何加焉！」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the attendant officials and said: "Sun Duo is an upright man—even the ancient Wei Zheng could not surpass him!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Sun Duo is a man of integrity. Even the great Wei Zheng of Tang could not surpass him!"

sentences.zh: 三年，御史中丞孫即康、刑部尚書賈鉉皆除參知政事，鐸再任戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year Investigating Censor-in-Chief Sun Jikang and Minister of Justice Jia Xuan were both appointed Vice Grand Councilors; Duo was again made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Sun Jikang was made Censor-in-Chief and Jia Xuan Minister of Justice, and both were appointed Vice Grand Councilors. Duo was again made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 鐸心少之，對賀客誦古人詩曰：「唯有庭前老柏樹，春風來似不曾來。

translations.literal: Duo inwardly slighted this and, facing congratulatory guests, recited an ancient poem: "Only the old cypress before the courtyard—when spring wind comes, it seems never to have come."
translations.idiomatic: Duo took the appointments poorly. When guests came to congratulate him, he quoted an old poem: "Only the old cypress before the courtyard—when the spring wind comes, it seems never to have come."

sentences.zh: 」御史大夫卞劾鐸怨望，降同知河南府事。

translations.literal: " Censor-in-Chief Bian impeached Duo for resentment and he was demoted to Vice Administrator of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Bian impeached Duo for disloyal resentment, and he was demoted to Vice Administrator of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改彰化軍節度使，複為中都轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army and again became Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army and again Transport Commissioner of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taihe he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taihe he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 蒲陰縣令大中與左司郎中劉昂、通州刺史史肅、前臨察御史王宇、吏部主事曹元、戶部員外郎李著、監察御史劉國樞、尚書省都事曹溫、雄州都軍馬師周，吏部員外郎徒單永康、太倉使馬良顯、順州刺史唐括直思白坐私議朝政，下獄，尚書省奏其罪。

translations.literal: Puyin Magistrate Dazhong together with Left Bureau Director Liu Ang, Prefect of Tongzhou Shi Su, former Surveillance Censor Wang Yu, Principal Official of Personnel Cao Yuan, Vice Director of Revenue Li Zhu, Investigating Censor Liu Guoshu, Secretariat Chief Clerk Cao Wen, and Xiongzhou Commander Ma Shizhou; Vice Director of Personnel Tudan Yongkang, Taicang Commissioner Ma Liangxian, and Prefect of Shunzhou Tangguo Zhisi were convicted of privately discussing court affairs, imprisoned, and the Ministry of Revenue memorialized their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Puyin Magistrate Dazhong, Left Bureau Director Liu Ang, Prefect of Tongzhou Shi Su, former Surveillance Censor Wang Yu, Personnel Principal Official Cao Yuan, Revenue Vice Director Li Zhu, Investigating Censor Liu Guoshu, Secretariat Chief Clerk Cao Wen, Xiongzhou Commander Ma Shizhou, Personnel Vice Director Tudan Yongkang, Taicang Commissioner Ma Liangxian, and Prefect of Shunzhou Tangguo Zhisi were imprisoned for privately discussing court affairs. The Ministry of Revenue memorialized their crimes.

sentences.zh: 鐸進曰：「昂等非敢議朝政，但如鄭人遊鄉校耳。

translations.literal: Duo advanced and said: "Ang and the others did not dare discuss court affairs; it was only like the people of Zheng visiting the district school."
translations.idiomatic: Duo spoke up: "Ang and the others were not presuming to debate court policy. They were only like the people of Zheng airing opinions at the district school."

sentences.zh: 」上悟，乃薄其罪。

translations.literal: " The emperor understood and lightened their punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and lightened their sentences.

sentences.zh: 鐸上言：「民間鈔多，宜收斂。

translations.literal: Duo submitted: "Paper notes among the people are numerous; they should be collected and reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Duo memorialized: "Too much paper currency is in circulation among the people. It should be recalled and reduced."

sentences.zh: 院務課程及諸窠名錢須要全收交鈔。

translations.literal: The schedules of bureau duties and all named-category monies must be collected entirely in exchange notes.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau duties and all named-category revenues should be collected entirely in paper currency.

sentences.zh: 秋夏稅本色外，盡令折鈔，不拘貫例，農民知之，迤漸重鈔。

translations.literal: Beyond the autumn and summer taxes in kind, all should be converted to notes without regard to the standard string-count; when farmers know this, they will gradually value notes.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond autumn and summer taxes paid in kind, all should be converted to notes without fixed exchange rates. Once farmers understand this, they will come to rely on paper currency.

sentences.zh: 比來州縣抑配行市買鈔，無益，徒擾之耳。

translations.literal: Recently prefectures and districts have compelled allocation and forced the markets to buy notes—this is useless and only harasses people.
translations.idiomatic: Recently local governments have forced merchants to buy notes at assigned prices. This accomplishes nothing and only harasses the people.

sentences.zh: 乞罷諸處鈔局，惟省庫仍舊，小鈔無限路分，可令通行。

translations.literal: I beg that note bureaus everywhere be abolished, leaving only the provincial treasury as before; small notes without limit by circuit may be permitted to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that local note bureaus be abolished, leaving only the provincial treasury in operation, and that small-denomination notes be permitted to circulate freely across all circuits.

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏，即詔有司曰：「可速行之。

translations.literal: " The emperor reviewed the memorial and immediately decreed to the responsible offices: "This may be swiftly implemented."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and immediately ordered the responsible offices, "Put this into effect at once."

sentences.zh: 」大安初，議誅黃門李新喜。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Da'an there was discussion of executing the Yellow Gate attendant Li Xinxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Da'an era the court debated executing the palace attendant Li Xinxi.

sentences.zh: 鐸曰：「此先朝用之太過耳。

translations.literal: Duo said: "This is only because the previous reign used him excessively."
translations.idiomatic: Duo said, "This is only because the previous reign relied on him too heavily."

sentences.zh: 」衛紹王不察，即曰：「卿今日始言之何耶？

translations.literal: " Prince of Wei Shao, without understanding, immediately said: "Why do you speak of this only today?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Shao, missing the point, snapped, "Why do you raise this only now?"

sentences.zh: 」既而複曰：「後當盡言，勿以此介意。

translations.literal: " He then added: "Hereafter you should speak fully; do not take offense at this."
translations.idiomatic: He then added, "Speak your mind fully in future. Do not hold this against me."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，遷尚書左丞，兼修國史。

translations.literal: " Before long he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, concurrently compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat, with concurrent duty to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 議鈔法忤旨，猶以論李新喜降浚州防禦使。

translations.literal: Having opposed the emperor's will on the note law, and still for his discussion of Li Xinxi, he was demoted to Military Commissioner of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For opposing the emperor on currency policy and for his remarks about Li Xinxi, he was demoted to Military Commissioner of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 改安國軍節度使，徙絳陽軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and moved to Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of the Anguo Army and transferred to Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，召赴闕，以兵道阻。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded, he was summoned to court but was blocked by the military routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong came to the throne, Duo was summoned to court but could not reach the capital because the roads were blocked by warfare.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，鐸上謁於宜村，除太子太師。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Duo presented himself at Yicun and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Duo presented himself at Yicun and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 在疾，累遣使候問。

translations.literal: While ill, the emperor repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: While Duo lay ill, the emperor repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyou he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyou he retired.

sentences.zh: 是歲薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 孫即康

translations.literal: Sun Jikang
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jikang

sentences.zh: 初，張汝弼妻高陀斡不道，伏誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Rubi's wife Gaotuowo committed an offense against the Way and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Rubi's wife Gaotuowo was executed for treasonous conduct.

sentences.zh: 汝弼，鎬王永中舅也，上由是頗疑永中。

translations.literal: Rubi was the maternal uncle of Prince of Hao Yong Yongzhong; the emperor therefore came to suspect Yongzhong considerably.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi was the maternal uncle of Prince of Hao Yong Yongzhong, and the emperor came to view Yongzhong with deep suspicion.

sentences.zh: 永中府傅尉奏永中第四子阿離合懣語涉不軌，詔同簽大睦親府事袴與即康鞫之。

translations.literal: Yongzhong's Prefecture Instructor Wei memorialized that Yongzhong's fourth son Alige, in resentful speech, was involved in words touching on sedition; an edict ordered Co-signatory of the Great Mutual-Affection Princely Establishment Ku and Jikang to examine the case.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong's Prefecture Instructor Wei reported that the prince's fourth son Alige had spoken resentful words suggesting sedition. The court ordered Co-signatory of the Great Mutual-Affection Princely Establishment Ku and Jikang to investigate.

sentences.zh: 第二子神土門嘗撰詞曲，頗輕肆，遂以語涉不遜就逮。

translations.literal: The second son Shentumen had once composed song lyrics, rather frivolous and unrestrained, and was therefore arrested on grounds that his words touched on disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Shentumen had composed song lyrics of a frivolous and unrestrained character and was arrested on charges of disrespectful speech.

sentences.zh: 家奴德哥首永中嘗與侍妾瑞雲言：「我得天下，以爾為妃，子為大王。

translations.literal: Household slave Dege reported that Yongzhong had once said to his concubine Ruiyun: "If I obtain the realm, I will make you consort and my son a great king."
translations.idiomatic: The household slave Dege reported that Yongzhong had told his concubine Ruiyun, "If I win the realm, I will make you my consort and my son a great king."

sentences.zh: 」袴、即康還奏，詔禮部尚書張暐複訊。

translations.literal: " Ku and Jikang returned with their report; an edict ordered Minister of Rites Zhang Wei to conduct a further interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Ku and Jikang reported their findings, and the court ordered Minister of Rites Zhang Wei to conduct a further interrogation.

sentences.zh: 永中父子皆死，時論冤之。

translations.literal: Yongzhong and his sons all died; contemporary opinion held it a miscarriage of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong and his sons were all put to death, and public opinion held the case a grave injustice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷泰甯軍節度使，改知延安府事。

translations.literal: Before long Jikang was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Taining Army and made Administrator of Yan'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jikang was made Military Commissioner of the Taining Army and Administrator of Yan'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，上問宰相：「今漢官誰可用者？

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Cheng'an the emperor asked the chancellors: "Which Han officials are usable now?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Cheng'an the emperor asked his chancellors, "Which Han officials are fit for service now?"

sentences.zh: 」司空襄舉即康。

translations.literal: " Minister of Works Xiang recommended Jikang.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Xiang recommended Jikang.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不輕薄否？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is he not frivolous?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is he not rather frivolous?"

sentences.zh: 」襄曰：「可再用為中丞觀之。

translations.literal: " Xiang said: "He may be used again as Censor-in-Chief to observe him."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "Appoint him Censor-in-Chief again and observe his conduct."

sentences.zh: 」上乃複召即康為御史中丞。

translations.literal: " The emperor then again summoned Jikang as Investigating Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then recalled Jikang as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，除參知政事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 明年，進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: The following year he was advanced to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 六年，宋渝盟有端，大臣猶以為小盜竊發不足恤。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Song violated the treaty and there were incidents; the great ministers still regarded it as petty banditry not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Song violated the treaty and incidents followed, yet senior ministers still dismissed the trouble as petty banditry not worth concern.

sentences.zh: 即康與左丞僕散端、參政獨吉思忠以為必當用兵，上以為然。

translations.literal: Jikang together with Left Vice Minister Pusan Duan and Vice Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong held that military force must certainly be used; the emperor regarded this as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Jikang, Left Vice Minister Pusan Duan, and Vice Grand Councilor Duji Sizhong argued that war was unavoidable, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上問即康、參知政事賈鉉曰：「太宗廟諱同音字，有讀作'成'字者，既非同音，便不當缺點畫。
