translations.literal: The emperor asked Jikang and Vice Grand Councilor Jia Xuan: "For Emperor Taizong's temple taboo, homophones—some read as the character 'cheng'—since they are not homophones, dots and strokes should not be omitted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Jikang and Vice Grand Councilor Jia Xuan, "For Emperor Taizong's temple taboo, some homophone characters are read as cheng. Since they are not true homophones, their strokes should not be omitted."

sentences.zh: 睿宗廟諱改作'崇'字，其下卻有本字全體，不若將'示'字依《蘭亭貼》寫作'未'字。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong's temple taboo is altered to the character 'chong,' yet below it the full original character remains; it would be better to write the character 'shi' as 'wei' following the Lanting tie.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong's taboo character is written as chong, yet the full original form remains beneath it. It would be better to write shi as wei, following the Lanting Preface model.

sentences.zh: 顯宗廟諱'允'，'充'字合缺點畫，如'統'傍之'充'，似不合缺。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong's taboo is 'yun'; the character 'chong' should have dots and strokes omitted, but the 'chong' beside 'tong' in 'tong' seems not appropriate to omit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong's taboo is yun, and the character chong should have strokes omitted—but the chong in tong seems inappropriate to alter.

sentences.zh: 」即康奏曰：「唐太宗諱世民，偏傍犯如'{艸枼}'字作'筼'字，'泯'字作'泜'字。

translations.literal: " Jikang memorialized: "Emperor Taizong of Tang tabooed Shimin; for characters sharing components, such as one with grass and world components written as 'yun,' and 'min' written as 'zhi.'"
translations.idiomatic: Jikang memorialized, "Emperor Taizong of Tang tabooed the name Shimin. Characters sharing components were altered—for example, characters containing the world radical were written as yun, and min was written as zhi."

sentences.zh: 」乃擬「熙宗廟諱從'面'從'且'。

translations.literal: " He then drafted: "Emperor Xizong's temple taboo: follow 'face' and follow 'and.'"
translations.idiomatic: He drafted rules for Emperor Xizong's taboo using the components face and and.

sentences.zh: 睿宗廟諱上字從'未'，下字從'簹'。

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong's taboo: upper character follows 'wei,' lower character follows 'dang.'
translations.idiomatic: For Emperor Ruizong's taboo, the upper component should follow wei and the lower dang.

sentences.zh: 世宗廟諱從'系'。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong's taboo follows 'silk.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong's taboo follows the silk radical.

sentences.zh: 顯宗廟諱如正犯字形，止書斜畫，'沇'字'鈗'字各從'口'，'兌悅'之類各從本傳。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong's taboo like the form of the direct violation: only write a slanting stroke; 'yan' and 'yun' each follow 'mouth'; types such as 'dui' and 'yue' each follow the original transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong's taboo follows the direct form: only a slanting stroke is written. Yan and yun each use the mouth radical; characters such as dui and yue follow their standard forms.

sentences.zh: 」從之，自此不勝曲避矣。

translations.literal: " This was adopted; from this time taboo evasion could not be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his proposal, and from that point taboo evasion knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 進左丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 宋人請和，進官一階。

translations.literal: When the Song requested peace, he was advanced one rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song sued for peace, he was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 李革，字君美，河津人。

translations.literal: Li Ge, style name Junmei, was a native of Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ge, style name Junmei, came from Hejin.

sentences.zh: 父余慶，三至廷試，不遂，因棄去。

translations.literal: His father Yuqing reached the palace examination three times without success and therefore abandoned the pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuqing reached the palace examination three times without success and abandoned official life.

sentences.zh: 革穎悟，讀書一再誦，輒記不忘。

translations.literal: Ge was quick-witted; reading once or twice through a text, he would remember it without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was exceptionally quick-witted. After reading a text once or twice, he never forgot it.

sentences.zh: 大定二十五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-fifth year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 調真定主簿。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Registrar of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Registrar of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 察廉，遷韓城令。

translations.literal: Recognized for integrity, he was transferred to Magistrate of Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for integrity, he was made Magistrate of Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 同知州事納富商賂，以歲課軍須配屬縣，革獨不聽，提刑司以為能。

translations.literal: The Vice Prefect accepted bribes from wealthy merchants and allocated annual military requisitions to subordinate counties; Ge alone would not comply, and the surveillance commission regarded this as ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Prefect accepted bribes from wealthy merchants and allocated annual military levies to subordinate counties. Ge alone refused to comply, and the surveillance commission praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷河北東路轉運都勾判官、太原推官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Reviewing Clerk of Hebei East Circuit Transport and Judicial Reviewer of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Reviewing Clerk of Hebei East Circuit Transport and Judicial Reviewer of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複，遷大興縣令、中都左警巡使、南京提刑判官、監察御史、同知昭義軍節度事。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his mother he was recalled, and was transferred to Magistrate of Daxing, Left Patrol Commissioner of the Central Capital, Judicial Reviewer of the Southern Capital, Investigating Censor, and Vice Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was recalled and served successively as Magistrate of Daxing, Left Patrol Commissioner of the Central Capital, Judicial Reviewer of the Southern Capital, Investigating Censor, and Vice Commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複，簽南京按察事。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning for his father he was recalled and signed surveillance affairs of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his father he was recalled to sign surveillance affairs in the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，伐宋，尚書省奏：「軍興，隨路官，差占者別注，闕者選補，老不任職者替罷，及司、縣各存留強幹正官一員。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, when campaigning against Song, the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "With the army raised, officials along each route who are seconded should be separately noted, vacancies should be filled by selection, those old and unfit for office should be replaced and dismissed, and each bureau and county should retain one strong and capable regular official."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe, during the campaign against Song, the Ministry of Revenue memorialized: "With war underway, seconded officials along each route should be noted separately, vacancies filled by selection, incompetent elders replaced, and each bureau and county should retain one capable regular official."

sentences.zh: 」革與簽陝西高霖、簽山東孟子元俱被詔，體訪三路官員能否，籍存留正官，行省、行部、元帥府差占員數及事故闕員，老不任職，赴闕奏事。

translations.literal: " Ge together with Signatory of Shaanxi Gao Lin and Signatory of Shandong Meng Ziyuan were all ordered by edict to investigate the capability of officials on the three routes, register retained regular officials, the numbers seconded by regional commands, ministries on campaign, and marshal's headquarters, vacancies due to circumstances, and those old and unfit for office, and come to court to report.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, together with Signatory of Shaanxi Gao Lin and Signatory of Shandong Meng Ziyuan, were ordered to assess officials on the three routes, register retained regular posts, tally secondments by regional commands and marshal's headquarters, note vacancies and incompetent elders, and report to the court.

sentences.zh: 改刑部員外郎，調觀州刺史兼提舉漕運，陝西西路按察副使，大興府治中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, assigned Prefect of Guanzhou with concurrent charge of promoting transport, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi West Circuit, and Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice, then Prefect of Guanzhou with charge of transport, Deputy Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi West Circuit, and Administrator of Daxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知府徒單南平貴幸用事，勢傾中外，遣所親以進取誘革，革拒之。

translations.literal: Prefect Tudan Nanping, a favorite in power, dominated court and countryside; he sent a close associate to entice Ge with advancement, and Ge refused.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tudan Nanping, a powerful favorite, dominated the court. He sent an associate to entice Ge with promises of advancement, and Ge refused.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou he was made Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗遷汴，行河北西路六部事，遷知開封府事，河南勸農使，戶部、吏部尚書，陝西行省參議官。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved to Bian, he handled the six ministries of Hebei West Circuit, was transferred to Administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture in Henan, Minister of Revenue and Minister of Personnel, and Councilor of the Shaanxi Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong moved the capital to Bian, Ge handled the six ministries of Hebei West Circuit, then served as Administrator of Kaifeng, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture in Henan, Minister of Revenue, Minister of Personnel, and Councilor of the Shaanxi Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 革奏：「有司各以情見引用斷例，牽合附會，實啟幸門。

translations.literal: Ge memorialized: "The various offices each cite precedent according to personal inclination, forcing connections and associations—this truly opens the gate of favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: Ge memorialized, "Offices cite precedents according to personal inclination, forcing connections where none exist. This opens the door to favoritism."

sentences.zh: 乞凡斷例敕條特旨奏斷不為永格者，不許引用，皆以律為正。

translations.literal: I beg that all precedents, edict articles, and special imperial decisions that are not to serve as permanent standards may not be cited; the statutes alone should be taken as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that precedents, edict articles, and special imperial rulings not intended as permanent standards may not be cited. The code alone should govern.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大元兵破潼關，革自以執政失備禦之策，上表請罪。

translations.literal: That year Great Yuan troops broke through Tong Pass; Ge, considering himself as chief minister to have failed in policies of defense, submitted a memorial requesting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mongol troops broke through Tong Pass. Ge, believing that as chief minister he had failed in defense policy, submitted a memorial requesting punishment.

sentences.zh: 不許，罷為絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: This was not permitted; he was dismissed and made Military Commissioner of Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied, but he was dismissed and made Military Commissioner of Jiangyang.

sentences.zh: 興定元年，胥鼎自平陽移鎮陝西，革以知平陽府事，權參知政事，代鼎為河東行省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingding, Xu Ding moved from Pingyang to command Shaanxi; Ge, as Administrator of Pingyang Prefecture, was given acting Vice Grand Councilor and replaced Ding as Eastern Hebei Regional Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingding, Xu Ding transferred from Pingyang to command Shaanxi. Ge, as Administrator of Pingyang, was given acting Vice Grand Councilor and replaced Ding as commander of the Eastern Hebei Regional Command.

sentences.zh: 是時興兵伐宋，革上書曰：「今之計當休兵息民，養銳待敵。

translations.literal: At that time troops were raised to campaign against Song; Ge submitted a memorial saying: "The plan now should be to rest the armies and give the people peace, nurture sharpness and await the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then raised for a campaign against Song. Ge memorialized, "The wise course now is to rest the armies, give the people peace, and conserve strength while awaiting the enemy."

sentences.zh: 宋雖造釁，止可自備。

translations.literal: Although the Song have created provocation, we should only prepare ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Song have provoked us, we should only prepare our defenses.

sentences.zh: 若不忍小忿以勤遠略，恐或乘之，不能支也。

translations.literal: If we cannot bear a small grievance and mobilize for distant strategy, I fear another power may seize the opportunity and we will not be able to hold.
translations.idiomatic: If we cannot bear a small insult and launch a distant campaign, I fear another enemy may seize the opportunity and we will not hold.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " This was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not accept his counsel.

sentences.zh: 太原兵後闕食，革移粟七萬石以濟之。

translations.literal: After the warfare Taiyuan lacked food; Ge transferred seventy thousand shi of grain to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting Taiyuan faced famine. Ge transferred seventy thousand shi of grain to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 二年，宣差粘割梭失至河東，於是晚禾未熟，牒行省耕毀清野。

translations.literal: In the second year the imperial commissioner Nianka Suoshi arrived in Hedong; at that time the late rice was not yet ripe, and he issued a dispatch to the regional command to plow and destroy for scorched-earth clearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the imperial commissioner Nianka Suoshi arrived in Hedong. The late rice crop was not yet ripe, yet he ordered the regional command to plow under fields for a scorched-earth policy.

sentences.zh: 革奏：「今歲雨澤及時，秋成可待。

translations.literal: Ge memorialized: "This year rain and moisture came in season; the autumn harvest can be awaited."
translations.idiomatic: Ge memorialized, "This year the rains came in season. A harvest can still be expected."

sentences.zh: 如令耕毀，民將不堪。

translations.literal: If ordered to plow and destroy, the people will not be able to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: If the fields are plowed under, the people will not survive.

sentences.zh: 」詔從革奏。

translations.literal: " An edict followed Ge's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted Ge's memorial.

sentences.zh: 十月，平陽被圍，城中兵不滿六千，屢出戰，旬日間傷者過半。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Pingyang was besieged; troops in the city numbered fewer than six thousand; they sallied repeatedly, and within ten days more than half were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Pingyang was besieged. The garrison numbered fewer than six thousand. They sallied repeatedly, and within ten days more than half were wounded.

sentences.zh: 徵兵吉、隰、霍三州，不時至。

translations.literal: Troops were levied from the three prefectures of Ji, Xi, and Huo but did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements were summoned from Ji, Xi, and Huo prefectures but did not arrive in time.

sentences.zh: 裨將李懷德縋城出降，兵自城東南入。

translations.literal: Vice General Li Huaide was lowered by rope from the wall to surrender; troops entered from the southeast of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Li Huaide was lowered over the wall to surrender, and enemy troops entered from the southeast.

sentences.zh: 左右請革上馬突圍出，革歎曰：「吾不能保此城，何面目見天子！

translations.literal: Those beside him asked Ge to mount and break out; Ge sighed and said: "I could not preserve this city—what face have I to see the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants urged Ge to mount and break out. Ge sighed, "I could not hold this city. What face have I to show the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 汝輩可去矣。

translations.literal: You may all depart.
translations.idiomatic: You may all go.

sentences.zh: 」乃自殺。

translations.literal: " He then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 贈尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》曰：「君子之言，其利博哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: The Zuozhuan says: "The words of the gentleman—how broad their benefit!"
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Zuozhuan says, "The words of a gentleman benefit all broadly!"

sentences.zh: 」徒單鎰拱挹一語而宣宗立，厥功懋矣。

translations.literal: " With a single bowed phrase Tu Danyi established Xuanzong—his achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: With a single restrained phrase Tu Danyi secured Xuanzong's enthronement—no small achievement.

sentences.zh: 賈鉉、孫鐸皆舊臣，鉉久致仕，鐸忤旨衛王，皆不復見用。

translations.literal: Jia Xuan and Sun Duo were both old ministers; Xuan long retired, Duo offended Prince of Wei Shao's will—neither was again employed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xuan and Sun Duo were both veteran ministers. Xuan had long since retired; Duo had offended Prince of Wei Shao. Neither was employed again.

sentences.zh: 徒單鎰亦外官，惟孫即康詭隨，乃驟至宰相。

translations.literal: Tu Danyi also held external office; only Sun Jikang, crafty and compliant, suddenly reached the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Danyi too served in the provinces. Only Sun Jikang, crafty and compliant, rose suddenly to the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 古所謂鬥筲之人，即康之謂矣。

translations.literal: What the ancients called a man of peck and dipper measure—this describes Jikang.
translations.idiomatic: He was precisely what the ancients called a man of small measure and narrow capacity.

sentences.zh: 鐸論李新喜，其言似漢耿育，有旨哉。

translations.literal: When Duo discussed Li Xinxi, his words resembled those of Geng Yu of Han—how pointed!
translations.idiomatic: Duo's remarks on Li Xinxi recall the Han minister Geng Yu—how pointed they were.

sentences.zh: 貞祐執政李革，可謂君子，其進退之際，有古人為相之風焉。

translations.literal: Li Ge, chief minister in Zhenyou, may be called a gentleman; in his advance and withdrawal there was the manner of the ancients in serving as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ge, chief minister in the Zhenyou era, may truly be called a gentleman. In how he held office and how he left it, he showed the bearing of the great chancellors of antiquity.
